Advances: ancora.review

Severity: Low (calibrated). Consolidated findings F31, F32, F62, F64, F66. Cannot have landed on the shipped branch: NOTICE and docs were outside the blocker tickets allowed touches, and the asset digests need a new standing test.

F31 — assert sha256 digests of all ten vendored Prism assets in review_assets_test.exs, so an unreviewed change to a vendored file fails CI. Today nothing pins their contents. Upgrade past 1.29.0 on the next touch of that directory.
F32 — NOTICE line 95 still reads json, html, css and javascript grammars only, while ancora.review.prism_carried now says markup. The vendored file is prism-markup.min.js, which registers the markup grammar and aliases html, xml, svg, mathml, rss, atom and ssml; Prism ships no prism-html.min.js. Reword NOTICE and the requirement so they agree and both state what is true: core Prism supplies markup, css and javascript, and these seven component files supply the rest. review_assets_test.exs only checks that NOTICE contains the string PrismJS 1.29.0, so nothing catches this drift.
F62 — five of the six priv/spec_init templates carry a .eex extension with no tags in them, yet all six go through EEx.eval_file, so a future literal opening EEx tag in that markdown would crash or evaluate. Rename the five tag-free templates to plain .md and .yml and copy them with File.cp!, keeping EEx.eval_file for AGENTS.md.eex alone, which has the one real tag.
F64 — republish the 30-code table in docs/migration.md with a default-severity column. The broader config-schema and Spec-Ack grammar documentation is deliberately NOT taken here.
F66 — give Git.read_blob/2 no-port fallback the same stderr separation the batch port has, so a git warning cannot be prepended into blob content. Add a comment at base_view.ex:52 recording that path-traversal safety depends on read_blob resolving through the git rev-colon-path form, so a future bulk-read optimization does not silently remove it. The security reviewer built a working proof-of-concept for that traversal: git mktree does accept a dot-dot entry and ls-tree -r emits it, and the chain reaches BaseView.materialize through a hostile default_base, but every blob read goes through rev-colon-path and git refuses to resolve dot-dot, so it dies before any write. The defense is real and undocumented.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/review_assets_test.exs (sha256 digests for all ten vendored files; NOTICE and ancora.review.prism_carried agree on the grammar list), test/ancora/scaffold/templates_test.exs and test/ancora/scaffold/fresh_adopter_test.exs (renamed templates copied verbatim, only AGENTS.md.eex evaluated), test/ancora/scaffold/docs_test.exs (migration table has a default-severity column), test/ancora/git_test.exs (read_blob no-port fallback separates stderr)
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) an unreviewed byte change to any vendored Prism asset fails CI; (2) NOTICE and the requirement both state that core Prism supplies markup, css, and javascript and the seven component files supply the rest; (3) five tag-free templates are plain .md and .yml copied with File.cp!, AGENTS.md.eex is the only EEx.eval_file; a literal EEx tag in a markdown template no longer evaluates; (4) docs/migration.md's 30-code table has a default-severity column matching lib/ancora/finding.ex; (5) a git warning cannot be prepended into blob content on the no-port path, and base_view.ex carries the comment recording that traversal safety depends on the rev-colon-path read
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: vendored asset bytes are pinned, NOTICE matches the requirement, and only AGENTS.md.eex goes through EEx.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- priv/spec_review_assets/** (only when upgrading past 1.29.0 in the same touch; digests must then be re-pinned and NOTICE updated)
- priv/spec_init/** (renames), lib/ancora/init.ex (copy vs evaluate)
- lib/ancora/git.ex (read_blob stderr separation), lib/ancora/base_view.ex (comment only)
- NOTICE, docs/migration.md, README.md
- test/ancora/review_assets_test.exs, test/ancora/scaffold/**, test/ancora/git_test.exs, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md (prism_carried wording; substantive), .spec/specs/ancora.scaffold.spec.md (template names)

- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. This list already permits lib/ancora/base_view.ex, lib/ancora/git.ex, which ancora.derive governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

- .spec/decisions/** (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator, third instance of the same admission defect, this one found by the ancora-xla.4 verifier. Ancora.PolicyFiles.missing_decision?/1 at lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:115 fires change/missing_decision whenever any path under .spec/specs/ changes without an accompanying decision-record change in the SAME diff. Every ticket here is required to edit a spec, so this finding is structurally guaranteed and the decision-record edit is forced rather than optional. Write a real contract statement describing what you actually built; do NOT add a hollow line to silence the finding, which a grader will read as finding-silencing and bounce.)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/review/html.ex (ancora-xla.4)
- lib/ancora/gate*
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- .spec/config.yml

Out of Scope (intent):
- no removal of the seven component grammars (dropped by the review)
- no config-schema or Spec-Ack grammar documentation beyond the severity column (explicitly not taken)
- no change to BaseView.materialize behavior; the comment documents a defense that already holds

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission ends result=pass
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket


SCOPE ADDITION (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 19:55). NOTICE line 42 describes the append-only guards and says "authorization is an accepted ADR whose affects: names the requirement or its subject". ancora-v1n makes that false: a subject id no longer authorizes anything. Since this ticket already owns reconciling NOTICE with what the code actually does, correct that line here so the bytes shipped match the behaviour shipped.

The sibling occurrence, the user-facing remediation hints at lib/ancora/finding.ex:234 and :239, is assigned to ancora-n24. Found by the ancora-v1n re-verification, which swept beyond its own scope.

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:
- Behaviors to demonstrate (5), lib/ancora/base_view.ex:67-68. The comment reads "Traversal safety depends on read_blob resolving through rev:path. Git rejects tree entries containing `..` before this code writes them." The second sentence is false, and the safety property it names does not exist. The ticket's premise, that git refuses to resolve dot-dot through the rev-colon-path form, does not hold on git 2.49.0. I built the tree by hand with plumbing and ran it:
  - `git mktree` accepts an entry named `..` at any depth, and `git ls-tree -r` emits the joined path. Both match the ticket's account.
  - `git show <rev>:sub/..` returns the blob with exit 0. `git show <rev>:a/../../evil.txt`, built from three nested trees whose entries are named `..`, also returns the blob with exit 0. `git cat-file --batch` resolves both identically, so the batch port path is affected too, not just the no-port fallback.
  - End to end through production code: `Ancora.BaseView.blobs/2` against that commit returned `%{"a/../../evil.txt" => "PWNED-ESCAPED\n"}`, and `Ancora.BaseView.materialize/2` wrote evil.txt one directory ABOVE its own materialized root. With TMPDIR pinned to a sandbox, the root was <sandbox>/tmp/ancora_base_view_31716_2018 and the file landed at <sandbox>/tmp/evil.txt. Path.join/2 does not normalize `..`, File.mkdir_p! creates the intermediate `a` so the OS resolves the traversal, and File.write! follows it out.
  - Reachable from the gate: BaseView.materialize is called at lib/ancora/gate.ex:67 and lib/ancora/review.ex:41, via the same hostile-default_base chain the ticket already accepts.
  The diff therefore ships a false safety claim in production source, and per this ticket's own framing a false comment about traversal safety is worse than no comment. The fix is a scope question for the orchestrator, not for me: either drop the safety assertion and record the real state, or add explicit path rejection in read_tree_blobs or materialize. The latter changes BaseView behaviour, which this ticket's Out of Scope (intent) forbids, so this likely needs a new ticket and the Out-of-Scope line's premise revisited.

Notes:
- Everything except that comment verifies cleanly. The digests, the renames, the NOTICE corrections, the severity table and the stderr separation are all correct and genuinely covered.
- The review_assets test's assertion on the spec's exact line wrapping is brittle. Advisory only.

ORCHESTRATOR NOTE before audit: I reproduced part of this and could NOT reproduce the decisive part (2026-09-03 21:10). Routing to audit rather than acting on it, and NOT reporting a vulnerability to Manuel until it is settled.

What I confirmed, on git 2.49.0, in a scratch repo:
- git mktree ACCEPTS a tree entry literally named '..'. It does not reject it.
- git ls-tree -r emits the joined path, so BaseView would iterate an entry whose path is 'a/..' or '../evil.txt'.
- git cat-file --batch RESOLVES '<commit>:a/..' and returns the blob header and payload, exit 0.

So the comment added at lib/ancora/base_view.ex:67-68 is FALSE as written. Git does not reject tree entries containing '..' before this code writes them. That alone justifies the FAIL, and it is what this ticket's own instruction called a Gap rather than a Note.

What I could NOT reproduce is the escape itself, which is the part that would make this a security issue rather than a documentation defect:
- I built a top-level tree entry named '..' containing evil.txt. ls-tree -r emits '../evil.txt', exactly the shape that would escape on write, and Path.join('/tmp/ancora-base-ROOT', '../evil.txt') does expand to /tmp/evil.txt.
- But git cat-file --batch REFUSES that path: 'fatal: ../evil.txt is outside repository'. So the read never returns content for the one path shape that would escape the write root.
- The form git DOES resolve, 'a/..', joins to root/a/.. which expands back to the root itself, a directory. File.write! there fails rather than escaping.

So on my evidence the two properties do not line up: the paths git will read do not escape, and the path that would escape git will not read. I may be missing the combination that does both. A three-level shape like 'a/../../evil.txt' is the obvious candidate and I did not construct it.

AUDITOR: settle this, and be specific about which of us is wrong. The verifier states it ran the real production functions and observed materialize/2 write a file one directory above its own root. If that is right, my reproduction is incomplete and I want the exact tree shape and the exact read that succeeded. If it is wrong, say so plainly: this epic has already had three claims disproved by re-measurement, and a false security report costs more than a missed one here because it would go to Manuel as a vulnerability.

Either way the FAIL stands on the comment alone. What the audit decides is the REMEDY, and that is a scope call:
- If there is no reachable escape, the fix is small and belongs in this ticket: delete or correct the two comment lines. Do not assert a safety property this code does not have; saying nothing is better.
- If there IS a reachable escape, the fix is NOT this ticket. Adding real path rejection changes BaseView.materialize behaviour, which this ticket's Out of Scope forbids on the premise that the defence already holds. That premise being wrong is exactly why it needs its own ticket, filed with a reproduction, and flagged to Manuel as security-relevant. Say so and I will file it.

Everything else in this diff verified clean by execution rather than by reading, and that work stands regardless: all ten vendored digests recomputed and matching, the scaffold renames proved by running mix spec.init with a deliberate literal-tag probe and revert, AGENTS.md.eex confirmed as the only remaining EEx path, the git.ex stderr separation mutation-tested to show the corruption it prevents, 19 of 19 files in scope, no trailer, and spec.check result=pass.

One handoff the verifier surfaced, unrelated to the Gap: lib/ancora/append_only.ex:10-12 moduledoc still states the old subject-authorization rule and now contradicts the corrected NOTICE. That belongs with ancora-v1n's rule change, not here.

AUDIT: BOUNCE → implementer
Session: adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/adec463e-8b46-45af-8018-b1cd8b92afc5.jsonl

Reasoning: The escape is real and I reproduced it end to end through the production functions on git 2.49.0. The verifier is correct and the orchestrator's reproduction was incomplete in exactly the way it suspected: it never built the three-level shape. The comment at lib/ancora/base_view.ex:67-68 asserts a safety property the code does not have, so the FAIL stands, and the remedy here is the comment correction only because a real fix changes BaseView.materialize behaviour, which this ticket's Out of Scope (intent) forbids.

What is passed to git for a read vs what is passed for a write: they are the same string, and that is the whole point. The read is Ancora.Git.blob_spec/2 at lib/ancora/git.ex:79, "#{base}:#{path}", where path is the verbatim ls-tree -r -z entry from parse_ls_tree. The write is Path.join(temp_root, path) at lib/ancora/base_view.ex:53 with the same verbatim path. The two strings do not differ. What differs is the interpretation. Git walks "<rev>:<path>" as literal tree-entry names and never normalizes, so an entry named ".." matches by name. Path.join/2 also never normalizes, so the "" survives into the destination and the OS resolves it at File.write! time. Path.expand is never called and no prefix check exists anywhere between ls_tree_entries and File.write!.

Tree shapes tried (git 2.49.0, scratch repos built with mktree/commit-tree in my own scratchpad, since deleted):
- top-level entry named ".." holding evil.txt: ls-tree -r emits "../evil.txt"; git show <rev>:../evil.txt exits 128 "fatal: '../evil.txt' is outside repository"; cat-file --batch dies with the same message; join target would be <parent-of-root>/evil.txt but the read never returns. Matches the orchestrator.
- nested "a" -> entry named "..": ls-tree -r emits nothing for it alone (a tree, not a blob); git show <rev>:a/.. exits 0 and returns the ROOT TREE listing, not a blob; join target is root/a/.. which expands back to root, a directory, so File.write! would fail. Matches the orchestrator.
- three-level "a" -> ".." -> ".." -> evil.txt: ls-tree -r emits "a/../../evil.txt"; git show <rev>:a/../../evil.txt exits 0 and returns "PWNED-ESCAPED\n"; git cat-file --batch resolves it identically, "c178f44c blob 14" followed by the payload; join target Path.expand(root <> "/a/../../evil.txt") is <parent-of-root>/evil.txt. This is the shape that does both, and it is the one nobody had constructed.
- five-level "a" -> ".." x5 -> pwned-deep.txt: ls-tree -r emits "a/../../../../../pwned-deep.txt", reads with exit 0, and lands five directories above the materialized root. Depth is attacker-chosen, so the write target is arbitrary, not just a sibling of the root.
- "./a/../../evil.txt": exit 128 "outside repository". "a/./../../evil.txt": exit 128 "path does not exist in <commit>". These two pin the mechanism. Git applies working-tree-relative resolution, which normalizes and rejects escapes, ONLY when the path string starts with "./" or "../". Anything else is a literal component-by-component tree walk, which is why an embedded ".." resolves and a leading one does not, and why a literal "." component fails for want of an entry named ".".

Escape reachable: YES. End-to-end evidence, running the real functions under mix run with TMPDIR pinned to a sandbox:
- Ancora.BaseView.blobs/3 on the hostile commit, no-port path, returned {:ok, %{"a/../../evil.txt" => "PWNED-ESCAPED\n", "ok.txt" => "benign\n"}}.
- The same call through a live RunContext with batch_port open returned byte-identical content, so lib/ancora/git.ex:64 (BatchPort) and lib/ancora/git.ex:72 (git show) are both affected. This is not a no-port-fallback-only issue.
- Ancora.BaseView.materialize/3 returned root <sandbox>/tmp/ancora_base_view_82134_2339 and wrote <sandbox>/tmp/evil.txt containing "PWNED-ESCAPED\n", one directory above its own root. File.mkdir_p! at base_view.ex:54 creates the intermediate "a" so the kernel has a real directory to walk up from, and File.write! at :55 follows it out.
- With the five-level tree the write landed at <sandbox>/l1/pwned-deep.txt, five levels above the root.
- The escaped file SURVIVES cleanup. gate.ex:67 and review.ex:41 both wrap materialize in File.rm_rf(base_root); I ran that rm_rf and the escaped file still existed afterward, because it was never inside base_root.
- Reachability: BaseView.materialize(ctx) at lib/ancora/gate.ex:67 and lib/ancora/review.ex:41, over whatever base the run resolved, via the hostile-default_base chain this ticket already accepts. No pathspec narrowing is passed at either site.

Who was right: the VERIFIER, on the decisive point. Its report is accurate as written, including the claim that blobs/2 returns an escaped path and materialize/2 writes above its own root. The ORCHESTRATOR was right about both shapes it actually tested and correctly identified the gap in its own work: the three-level shape it named as the obvious candidate and did not build is precisely the one that works. Nothing in the orchestrator's note is factually wrong; it is incomplete.

Bounce reason: implementer, comment correction only, and nothing else. Delete the two lines at lib/ancora/base_view.ex:67-68, or replace them with a statement that is true. The second sentence, "Git rejects tree entries containing `..` before this code writes them", is false and must not ship. The first sentence is also misleading, since traversal safety does not depend on the rev:path form and no such safety exists. If a replacement comment is wanted, it must record the real state, that entry paths are used verbatim for both the read and the write and are not validated. Saying nothing is acceptable and preferable to saying something false. This ticket's Allowed touches permit lib/ancora/base_view.ex for a COMMENT ONLY, so the correction is in scope; adding path rejection is not. Do not touch anything else in the diff. Everything else verified clean by execution and I did not re-audit it.

Separate security ticket required: YES. Arbitrary-path file write in Ancora.BaseView.materialize when the base commit's tree contains entries literally named "..", reachable from lib/ancora/gate.ex:67 and lib/ancora/review.ex:41, affecting both the batch port and the git show fallback, with the written file surviving the gate's own File.rm_rf cleanup. Reproduction: build three nested trees whose entries are named ".." with a blob at the bottom, commit-tree them under a directory entry, and point a run at that commit; ls-tree -r emits "a/../../evil.txt", both read paths resolve it with exit 0, and Path.join plus File.write! at lib/ancora/base_view.ex:53-55 put the content outside the materialized root. Add "../" levels to reach any depth. The remedy belongs in read_tree_blobs or materialize, which this ticket's Out of Scope (intent) forbids on the premise that the defence already holds, and that premise is exactly what is wrong. The cheapest fix consistent with this epic's less-machinery principle is a plain rejection in read_tree_blobs: drop or error on any entry whose path splits into a ".." component, no new module, no process, no cache. Orchestrator to file it and flag it to the repository owner. I did not file it.
